themes.evidence: Reuters reports markets assign roughly an 80% probability to a December Fed hike, while Fed officials Raphael Bostic and Beth Hammack favor gradual increases to reduce above-target inflation.
Fed Governor Christopher Waller said inflation remains the primary concern, while Reuters reported one-year US inflation expectations rose to 4.7% in October.
New York Fed President John Williams described US growth as remarkably resilient, and Reuters reported continued solid expansion supported partly by AI-infrastructure investment.
Reuters reported October job growth surged, unemployment fell to 4.1%, and the data reinforced expectations for a December Fed hike.
BofA FX strategist Alex Cohen said strong US growth and stubborn inflation could keep the dollar resilient for longer despite a broader forecast for depreciation.
Reuters said markets are increasingly focused on slowing growth alongside elevated inflation, raising concerns that central banks may need to tighten further.
Reuters reported markets price roughly a 60% chance of a December ECB hike, down from 75% the prior week, reflecting conflicting growth and inflation signals.
Reuters reported traders see a 58% probability that the Bank of Japan leaves rates unchanged next month, versus 42% odds of a hike.

Citi economist Jin-Wook Kim said downside risks to South Korean private consumption appear likely in the fourth quarter, while weaker memory prices and semiconductor exports could force a policy pause.
